model.rationale: Westerman is a well-funded incumbent in an R+20 district, while challenger James Russell has raised under $6,000 and markets give him about a 2% chance. Nothing in the evidence suggests movement away from a Safe R rating.
model.watch: Any unexpected incumbent scandal or late outside spending against Westerman would be the only plausible path to narrowing this race.

overview:
Bruce Westerman seeks another term in this southern Arkansas district, which leans about 20 points Republican at the baseline. He is a well-established incumbent with more than $4.6 million on hand after raising over $2.5 million this cycle. His Democratic opponent, James Russell, has raised roughly $5,900 and reports under $1,000 in the bank, leaving him with essentially no resources to compete.

No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, but prediction markets price Westerman's chances at about 98%. The district's strong Republican tilt, the incumbent's financial dominance, and the challenger's minimal campaign all point in the same direction, making this one of the least competitive House races on the ballot.
